overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by responding to a December 16 minutes request more than 10 calendar days later. The withholding challenge was resolved with no violation because the minutes were released in redacted form, and non-minutes documents were declined as Public Records Law matters.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to release unredacted executive session minutes in response to a December 16 request; the Board responded on December 31.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law with respect to the timeliness of its response.

allegations.summary: Complainant challenged the Board's withholding of the April 25 and May 7, 2019 executive session minutes under attorney-client privilege and a public records exemption.
allegations.key_passage: Because the executive session minutes at issue here are no longer being withheld from the public under the Open Meeting Law, we find no violation of that Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: To the extent the December 16 request sought documents other than meeting minutes, the AG declined review because those fall under the Public Records Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government may only review violations of the Open Meeting Law.
